Write the protocol as a trainer workout file

Source: R/protocol.R
write_workout.Rd

Turns comparison_protocol() into something a training app can ride, so the session is commanded rather than remembered. The format follows the file extension, the way read_file() dispatches on it.

Usage

write_workout(path, ftp = 250, protocol = comparison_protocol())

Arguments

path

File to write. The extension chooses the format: .zwo or .erg.

ftp

Functional threshold power in watts. .zwo stores targets as fractions of the rider's FTP, so this only reaches the description there; .erg stores absolute watts, where a wrong FTP is a wrong workout. The default is the package's reference rider; set your own.

protocol

A protocol from comparison_protocol().

Value

path, invisibly.

Details

.zwo (Zwift) carries the distinction the protocol depends on: erg steps are written as SteadyState and the sync surges and coasts as FreeRide, which releases erg control for exactly the blocks that must not be ridden in it. .erg (Golden Cheetah, TrainerDay, PerfPro) has no such concept and is a plain watts-against-time course, so the surge blocks come out as targets the trainer will try to hold. Drop out of erg for them by hand.

The trainer holding the targets must be commanded over ANT+: while the Record tab has the trainer's Bluetooth connection, nothing else can have it.

Examples

path <- tempfile(fileext = ".zwo")
write_workout(path, ftp = 250)
